# Spring Boot Web Application using Container Friendly Command Line Options

Java memory tuning is a complex and nuanced task, often requiring substantial
effort to achieve optimal performance. The process involves more than simply
setting a few parameters, as the optimal settings can vary significantly
between applications. Moreover, these settings may need to be adjusted whenever
new features are introduced or when there is a change in user behaviour.

Java provides several options to fine-tune the heap size based on the memory
allocated to a container. However, it is crucial to understand that the
`-Xmx###` parameter, which sets the maximum heap size, is static and does not
automatically adjust based on the container’s available memory.

Beyond heap memory, the Java Virtual Machine (JVM) utilizes additional memory
segments including:
- Stack Memory: Stores threads’ execution environment.
- Non-Heap Memory: Utilized for storing loaded classes, metadata, and other
  artefacts.
- Other JVM-specific memory: Includes the JVM code, internal structures, and any
  loaded profiler agent code and data.

To aid in monitoring and managing these memory uses, Java offers the
`-XX:NativeMemoryTracking=[off|summary|detail]` option. This feature is
instrumental for diagnosing memory leaks and understanding how memory is
allocated and used by the JVM and its applications.

Running Java applications in containers introduces additional considerations.
Containers can abruptly terminate applications that exceed allocated resources,
triggered by the Out of Memory (OOM) killer. This is particularly problematic
for Java applications if the JVM’s maximum memory settings exceed the limits set
by the container. It is essential for developers to ensure that JVM memory
settings are carefully aligned with container memory restrictions to avoid
unexpected terminations.

In this example we will see how to take advantage of all memory available to the
container and scale accordingly minimising the memory waste along the way. Java
predates containers and its defaults may not be adequate for running Java
applications inside a container.

This example is intentionally focused on one topic: configuring Java command
line options for container-aware memory sizing. It omits some
production-oriented container concerns, such as running as a non-root user,
image signing, vulnerability scanning, observability, and deployment-specific
hardening, so the JVM option behaviour remains easy to follow. For a more
complete Spring Boot container example that combines several concerns, see
[all-in-one-spring-boot](../all-in-one-spring-boot/).

This simple application has one endpoint that returns a random quote from its
database.

## Prerequisites

- [Oracle Java 25](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java25)

- [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/) runtime

- [Dive](https://github.com/wagoodman/dive), or other similar tool, to analyse
  the container image.

- [Oracle Account](https://profile.oracle.com/myprofile/account/create-account.jspx)
  to access [Oracle Container Registry](https://container-registry.oracle.com/)

- An Oracle Container Registry authentication token stored in
  `~/.ocr/auth-token`, or an equivalent secure way to pass the password to
  `docker login --password-stdin`.

## Adjust the memory usage

1. Determine the host memory

   The host memory is a key factor in determining default values.

   ```shell
   case "$(uname -s)" in
     Darwin)
       bytes=$(sysctl -n hw.memsize)
       echo "$((bytes / 1024 / 1024 / 1024))GB"
       ;;
     Linux)
       kb=$(awk '/^MemTotal:/ { print $2 }' /proc/meminfo)
       echo "$((kb / 1024 / 1024))GB"
       ;;
     *)
       echo "Unsupported OS: $(uname -s)" >&2
       exit 1
       ;;
   esac
   ```

   This machine has 32GB of RAM

   ```
   30GB
   ```

2. Determine Java default memory limits (using the `-XshowSettings:vm` and
   `-XX:+PrintFlagsFinal` options)

   ```shell
   java \
     -XshowSettings:vm \
     --version
   ```

   This will print the VM settings, which values vary depending on the version
   of Java and the host memory. Please note that the VM settings are printed to
   the stderr and not stdout.

   ```
   java 25.0.4.1 2026-08-18 LTS
   Java(TM) SE Runtime Environment (build 25.0.4.1+1-LTS-5)
   Java HotSpot(TM) 64-Bit Server VM (build 25.0.4.1+1-LTS-5, mixed mode, sharing)
   VM settings:
       Max. Heap Size (Estimated): 7.72G
       Using VM: Java HotSpot(TM) 64-Bit Server VM
   ```

   Note that the JVM adjusts the heap as 25% of the total memory when using the
   G1 GC. This is determined by the (*deprecated*) `MaxRAMFraction` option,
   which is set to `4` by default or the (*newer*) `MaxRAMPercentage` option
   which is set to `25%`.

   ```shell
   java \
     -XX:+PrintFlagsFinal \
     --version \
     | grep -Ei 'maxheapsize|maxram'
   ```

   The memory settings

   ```
      size_t MaxHeapSize                              = 8292139008                                {product} {ergonomic}
    uint64_t MaxRAM                                   = 137438953472                           {pd product} {default}
      double MaxRAMPercentage                         = 25.000000                                 {product} {default}
      size_t SoftMaxHeapSize                          = 8292139008                             {manageable} {ergonomic}
   ```

3. Adjust the memory limits using `-Xmx###`

   One option is to use the `-Xmx###` (and `-Xms###`) options to adjust the
   maximum heap valueNote that Java uses other memory, such as the stack
   (one per thread), while the `-Xmx###` option only limits the heap.

   ```shell
   java \
     -Xmx1G -Xms1G \
     -XshowSettings:vm \
     --version
   ```

   The Java version and VM settings

   ```
   java 25.0.4.1 2026-08-18 LTS
   Java(TM) SE Runtime Environment (build 25.0.4.1+1-LTS-5)
   Java HotSpot(TM) 64-Bit Server VM (build 25.0.4.1+1-LTS-5, mixed mode, sharing)
   VM settings:
       Min. Heap Size: 1.00G
       Max. Heap Size: 1.00G
       Using VM: Java HotSpot(TM) 64-Bit Server VM
   ```

   ```shell
   java \
     -Xmx1G -Xms1G \
     -XX:+PrintFlagsFinal \
     --version \
     | grep -Ei 'maxheapsize|maxram'
   ```

   The memory settings

   ```
      size_t MaxHeapSize                              = 1073741824                                {product} {command line}
    uint64_t MaxRAM                                   = 137438953472                           {pd product} {default}
      double MaxRAMPercentage                         = 25.000000                                 {product} {default}
      size_t SoftMaxHeapSize                          = 1073741824                             {manageable} {ergonomic}
   ```

4. Adjust the memory limits using `-XX:MaxRAMPercentage=###`

   The `-XX:MaxRAMPercentage=###` instructs Java to set the heap size a
   percentage of the available memory.

   ```shell
   java \
     -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75 \
     -XshowSettings:vm \
     --version
   ```

   The Java version and VM settings

   ```
   java 25.0.4.1 2026-08-18 LTS
   Java(TM) SE Runtime Environment (build 25.0.4.1+1-LTS-5)
   Java HotSpot(TM) 64-Bit Server VM (build 25.0.4.1+1-LTS-5, mixed mode, sharing)
   VM settings:
       Max. Heap Size (Estimated): 23.17G
       Using VM: Java HotSpot(TM) 64-Bit Server VM
   ```

   ```shell
   java \
     -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75 \
     -XX:+PrintFlagsFinal \
     --version \
     | grep -Ei 'maxheapsize|maxram'
   ```

   The memory settings

   ```
      size_t MaxHeapSize                              = 24880611328                               {product} {ergonomic}
    uint64_t MaxRAM                                   = 33166061568                            {pd product} {ergonomic}
      double MaxRAMPercentage                         = 75.000000                                 {product} {command line}
      size_t SoftMaxHeapSize                          = 24880611328                            {manageable} {ergonomic}
   ```

   Please note that `-Xmx###` takes precedence over `-XX:MaxRAMPercentage=##`.

   ```shell
   java \
     -Xmx1G -Xms1G \
     -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75 \
     -XshowSettings:vm \
     --version
   ```

   The Java version and VM settings

   ```
   java 25.0.4.1 2026-08-18 LTS
   Java(TM) SE Runtime Environment (build 25.0.4.1+1-LTS-5)
   Java HotSpot(TM) 64-Bit Server VM (build 25.0.4.1+1-LTS-5, mixed mode, sharing)
   ```


   The memory settings

   ```
      size_t MaxHeapSize                              = 1073741824                                {product} {command line}
    uint64_t MaxRAM                                   = 33166061568                            {pd product} {ergonomic}
      double MaxRAMPercentage                         = 75.000000                                 {product} {command line}
      size_t SoftMaxHeapSize                          = 1073741824                             {manageable} {ergonomic}
   ```

5. Adjust the memory limits using `-XX:MaxRAM=###`

   The `-XX:MaxRAM=###` sets the host memory limit for Java. When provided,
   Java will use this value as the host memory and will derive the other values
   based on this. For example, if the host has 16G of RAM, with `-XX:MaxRAM=4G`,
   Java limits the heap to 1G.

   ```shell
   java \
     -XX:MaxRAM=4G \
     -XshowSettings:vm \
     --version
   ```

   The Java version and VM settings

   ```
   java 25.0.4.1 2026-08-18 LTS
   Java(TM) SE Runtime Environment (build 25.0.4.1+1-LTS-5)
   Java HotSpot(TM) 64-Bit Server VM (build 25.0.4.1+1-LTS-5, mixed mode, sharing)
   VM settings:
       Max. Heap Size (Estimated): 1.00G
       Using VM: Java HotSpot(TM) 64-Bit Server VM
   ```

   ```shell
   java \
     -XX:MaxRAM=4G \
     -XX:+PrintFlagsFinal \
     --version \
     | grep -Ei 'maxheapsize|maxram'
   ```

   The memory settings

   ```
      size_t MaxHeapSize                              = 1073741824                                {product} {ergonomic}
    uint64_t MaxRAM                                   = 4294967296                             {pd product} {command line}
      double MaxRAMPercentage                         = 25.000000                                 {product} {default}
      size_t SoftMaxHeapSize                          = 1073741824                             {manageable} {ergonomic}
   ```

   Please note that `-Xmx###` takes precedence over `-XX:MaxRAM=##`.

   ```shell
   java \
     -Xmx512M -Xms512M \
     -XX:MaxRAM=4G \
     -XshowSettings:vm \
     --version
   ```

   The Java version and VM settings

   ```
   java 25.0.4.1 2026-08-18 LTS
   Java(TM) SE Runtime Environment (build 25.0.4.1+1-LTS-5)
   Java HotSpot(TM) 64-Bit Server VM (build 25.0.4.1+1-LTS-5, mixed mode, sharing)
   VM settings:
       Min. Heap Size: 512.00M
       Max. Heap Size: 512.00M
       Using VM: Java HotSpot(TM) 64-Bit Server VM
   ```

   ```shell
   java \
     -Xmx512M -Xms512M \
     -XX:MaxRAM=4G \
     -XX:+PrintFlagsFinal \
     --version \
     | grep -Ei 'maxheapsize|maxram'
   ```

   The memory settings

   ```
      size_t MaxHeapSize                              = 536870912                                 {product} {command line}
    uint64_t MaxRAM                                   = 4294967296                             {pd product} {command line}
      double MaxRAMPercentage                         = 25.000000                                 {product} {default}
      size_t SoftMaxHeapSize                          = 536870912                              {manageable} {ergonomic}
   ```

## Containers

1. Determine the memory available to the container

   The `free` command cannot be used from within the container to determine the
   amount of memory available to the container.

   ```shell
   docker run \
     --rm \
     --memory=1G \
     container-registry.oracle.com/java/jdk:25.0.4.1 \
     free
   ```

   This yields the amount of memory available to the node.

   ```
                  total        used        free      shared  buff/cache   available
   Mem:        32388732     2340604     1402096       18088    29154460    30048128
   Swap:        5350396           0     5350396
   ```

   The memory available in a container can be determined from the control groups
   (cgroup) file: `/sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max`.

   ```shell
   docker run \
     --rm \
     --memory=1G \
     container-registry.oracle.com/java/jdk:25.0.4.1 \
     cat /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max
   ```

   This prints 1G (in bytes value).

   ```
   1073741824
   ```

   You can round that and print the value in GB.

   ```shell
   echo "$(expr $(docker run --rm --memory=1G container-registry.oracle.com/java/jdk:25.0.4.1 cat /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max | sed 's/\r//g') / $((1024**3)))GB"
   ```

   This prints the same value in GB.

   ```
   1GB
   ```

   ![Container Memory](./assets/images/Container%20Memory.png)

2. Determine Java default memory limits (using the `-XshowSettings:vm` and
   `-XX:+PrintFlagsFinal` options)

   ```shell
   docker run \
     --rm \
     --memory=1G \
     container-registry.oracle.com/java/jdk:25.0.4.1 \
     java \
     -XshowSettings:vm \
     --version
   ```

   This will print the VM settings, which values vary depending on the version
   of Java and the container memory.

   ```
   java 25.0.4.1 2026-08-18 LTS
   Java(TM) SE Runtime Environment (build 25.0.4.1+1-LTS-5)
   Java HotSpot(TM) 64-Bit Server VM (build 25.0.4.1+1-LTS-5, mixed mode, sharing)
   VM settings:
       Max. Heap Size (Estimated): 247.50M
       Using VM: Java HotSpot(TM) 64-Bit Server VM
   ```

   Note that when using the G1 GC, the JVM adjusts the heap as 25% of the total
   memory.

   ![Default Heap Size](./assets/images/Default%20Heap%20Size.png)

   This is determined by the (*deprecated*) `MaxRAMFraction` option, which is
   set to `4` by default or the (*newer*) `MaxRAMPercentage` option which is set
   to `25%`.

   ```shell
   docker run \
     --rm \
     --memory=1G \
     container-registry.oracle.com/java/jdk:25.0.4.1 \
     java \
     -XX:+PrintFlagsFinal \
     --version \
     | grep -Ei 'maxheapsize|maxram'
   ```

   This will print the VM settings, which values vary depending on the version
   of Java and the container memory.

   ```
      size_t MaxHeapSize                              = 268435456                                 {product} {ergonomic}
    uint64_t MaxRAM                                   = 137438953472                           {pd product} {default}
      double MaxRAMPercentage                         = 25.000000                                 {product} {default}
      size_t SoftMaxHeapSize                          = 268435456                              {manageable} {ergonomic}
   ```

3. Adjust the memory limits using `-Xmx###`

   One option is to use the `-Xmx###` (and `-Xms###`) options to adjust the
   maximum heap value. Note that Java uses other memory, such as the stack
   (one per thread), while the `-Xmx###` option only limits the heap.

   ```shell
   docker run \
     --rm \
     --memory=1G \
     container-registry.oracle.com/java/jdk:25.0.4.1 \
     java \
     -Xmx512M -Xms512M \
     -XshowSettings:vm \
     --version
   ```

4. Adjust the memory limits using `-XX:MaxRAMPercentage=###`

   The `-XX:MaxRAMPercentage=###` instructs Java to set the heap size a
   percentage of the available memory.

   ```shell
   docker run \
     --rm \
     --memory=1G \
     container-registry.oracle.com/java/jdk:25.0.4.1 \
     java \
     -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75 \
     -XshowSettings:vm \
     --version
   ```

   The Java version and VM settings

   ```
   java 25.0.4.1 2026-08-18 LTS
   Java(TM) SE Runtime Environment (build 25.0.4.1+1-LTS-5)
   Java HotSpot(TM) 64-Bit Server VM (build 25.0.4.1+1-LTS-5, mixed mode, sharing)
   VM settings:
       Max. Heap Size (Estimated): 742.44M
       Using VM: Java HotSpot(TM) 64-Bit Server VM
   ```

   Different from `-Xmx`, the memory will scale with the container size. The
   heap will take 75% of the total available memory, which leaves enough space
   for the other things happening in the container, including Java itself.

   ![Set Heap Size though MaxRAMPercentage](./assets/images/Set%20Heap%20Size%20though%20MaxRAMPercentage.png)

   This scales with the container’s memory provides all available memory to the
   heap, while allowing enough memory for the other things to function.

   ![Set Heap Size though MaxRAMPercentage scale with container](./assets/images/Set%20Heap%20Size%20though%20MaxRAMPercentage%20scale%20with%20container.png)

   Please note that the `-XX:MaxRAMPercentage` option takes precedence over
   `-XX:MaxRAMFraction` option.

   ```shell
   docker run \
     --rm \
     --memory=1G \
     container-registry.oracle.com/java/jdk:25.0.4.1 \
     java \
     -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75 \
     -XX:+PrintFlagsFinal \
   ```


   The memory settings

   ```
      size_t MaxHeapSize                              = 268435456                                 {product} {command line}
    uint64_t MaxRAM                                   = 536870912                              {pd product} {command line}
      double MaxRAMPercentage                         = 25.000000                                 {product} {default}
      size_t SoftMaxHeapSize                          = 268435456                              {manageable} {ergonomic}
   ```

## Older versions of Java 8

Older versions of Java 8 do not detect the memory allocated to the container and
instead use the whole memory available to the container runtime, 8G in my case.

```shell
docker run \
  --rm \
  --memory=1G \
  container-registry.oracle.com/java/serverjre:8u351 \
  java \
  -XshowSettings:vm \
  -version
```

Java believes that more memory if available and will trigger the Out-of-Memory
killer once it utilises more memory that what was allocated to the container.

```
VM settings:
    Max. Heap Size (Estimated): 6.86G
    Ergonomics Machine Class: server
    Using VM: Java HotSpot(TM) 64-Bit Server VM

java version "1.8.0_351"
Java(TM) SE Runtime Environment (build 1.8.0_351-b10)
Java HotSpot(TM) 64-Bit Server VM (build 25.351-b10, mixed mode)
```

This limitation can be addressed with the `-XX:MaxRAM`, but
**it is recommended to use the latest version of Java instead** as this version
is considered insecure.

```shell
docker run \
  --rm \
  --memory=1G \
  container-registry.oracle.com/java/serverjre:8u351 \
  java \
  -XX:MaxRAM=1G \
  -XshowSettings:vm \
  -version
```

Java uses the value provided by `-XX:MaxRAM=###` to determine the maximum heap
size instead of relaying on the underlying OS (container).

```
VM settings:
    Max. Heap Size (Estimated): 228.00M
    Ergonomics Machine Class: server
    Using VM: Java HotSpot(TM) 64-Bit Server VM

java version "1.8.0_351"
Java(TM) SE Runtime Environment (build 1.8.0_351-b10)
Java HotSpot(TM) 64-Bit Server VM (build 25.351-b10, mixed mode)
```

Java 8 Update 361 (**which is still old and considered insecure**) addressed
this limitation.

```shell
docker run \
  --rm \
  --memory=1G \
  container-registry.oracle.com/java/serverjre:8u361 \
  java \
  -XshowSettings:vm \
  -version
```

The heap is allocated only 25% of the memory available to the container.

```
VM settings:
    Max. Heap Size (Estimated): 247.50M
    Ergonomics Machine Class: server
    Using VM: Java HotSpot(TM) 64-Bit Server VM

java version "1.8.0_361"
Java(TM) SE Runtime Environment (build 1.8.0_361-b09)
Java HotSpot(TM) 64-Bit Server VM (build 25.361-b09, mixed mode)
```

**It is imperative to migrate to the latest version of Java 8**.

## Enterprise Performance Pack

This section demonstrates how to build a container image based on Enterprise
Performance Pack (EPP) and load into the local container registry. For a
comprehensive description of how to create a multi-platform container image for
EPP, please refer to the
[Create a multi-platform container image with Java SE Subscription Enterprise Performance Pack](https://inside.java/2023/06/12/multiplatform-containers-javaepp/)
article.

1. Download EPP from the
   [Oracle Java Downloads page](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#jepp).

   Save the RPM file under the `./containers/binaries` directory.

   Verify that the RPM file is under the `./containers/binaries` directory.

   ```shell
   tree -P '*.rpm' './containers'
   ```

   The EPP RPM.

   ```
   ./containers
   └── binaries
       ├── jdk-8u491-perf-linux-aarch64.rpm
       └── jdk-8u491-perf-linux-x64.rpm

   2 directories, 2 files
   ```

2. Build the container image

   ```shell
   docker build \
     --file './containers/Dockerfile-EPP' \
     --tag 'epp:491' \
     --load \
     './containers'
   ```

   (*Optional*) Verify that the image is loaded in the local container
   registry.

   ```shell
   docker image list epp
   ```

   The images in the local repository

   ```
   REPOSITORY     TAG         IMAGE ID      CREATED       SIZE
   localhost/epp  491         d844573a8d7e  1 second ago  400 MB
   ```

3. Run the container image

   ```shell
   docker run \
     --rm \
     --memory=1G \
     epp:491 \
     java \
     -XshowSettings:vm \
     -version
   ```

   EPP is able to detect the container limits and adjusts accordingly.

   ```
   VM settings:
       Max. Heap Size (Estimated): 247.50M
       Ergonomics Machine Class: server
       Using VM: Java HotSpot(TM) 64-Bit Server VM

   java version "1.8.0_491"
   Java(TM) SE Runtime Environment (build 1.8.0_491-perf-37-b08)
   Java HotSpot(TM) 64-Bit Server VM (build 17.0.19+8-perf-37, mixed mode, sharing)
   ```

## Running a Spring Boot Application

1. Build application

   ```shell
   ./mvnw clean verify
   ```

   (*Optional*) Verify that the JAR file was created.

   ```shell
   tree -P '*.jar' --prune './target'
   ```

   The application JAR file

   ```
   ./target
   └── java-command-line-options-spring-boot-1.0.0.jar

   1 directory, 1 file
   ```

2. Review the (adjusted heap) container file
   (`./containers/Dockerfile-Adjusted-Heap`)

   The container applies the JVM options through the `JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS`
   environment variable. This keeps the image entrypoint focused on the
   application launch command while still making the JVM options visible in the
   container definition.

   The JVM options are:

   - `-XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75.0`: sets the maximum Java heap as a percentage of
     the memory available to the JVM. In this example, the maximum heap can grow
     up to 75% of the container memory limit.
   - `-XX:MinRAMPercentage=75.0`: sets the minimum heap percentage used by JVM
     ergonomics for small memory sizes. It does not reserve all container memory
     for the heap, and it should not be treated as a replacement for deliberate
     `-Xms` sizing.
   - `-XshowSettings:vm`: prints VM settings during startup. This is useful in
     the workshop because it shows the computed heap size, but it is usually a
     diagnostic option rather than a production logging default.

   The 75% value is a sensible demonstration default, but production values
   should be validated with the application workload because heap memory is only
   part of the process memory used by the JVM.

   ```dockerfile
   FROM container-registry.oracle.com/java/jdk:25.0.4.1
   WORKDIR /opt/app

   ARG JAR_FILE=./target/java-command-line-options-spring-boot-1.0.0.jar

   COPY ${JAR_FILE} app.jar

   ENV JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS="-XX:MinRAMPercentage=75.0 -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75.0 -XshowSettings:vm"

   ENTRYPOINT ["java", "-jar", "app.jar"]
   ```

3. Build the (adjusted heap) container image

   ```shell
   docker build \
     --file './containers/Dockerfile-Adjusted-Heap' \
     --tag 'demo:adjusted-heap' \
     --load \
     .
   ```

4. Run the container image

   ```shell
   docker run \
     --rm \
     --detach \
     --memory=1G \
     --name 'adjusted-heap' \
     --publish 8080:8080 \
     'demo:adjusted-heap'
   ```

   Verify the amount of heap memory available to the application.

   ```shell
   docker logs 'adjusted-heap' | head
   ```

   This application is using 75% of the container’s memory.

   ```
   NOTE: Picked up JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS: -XX:MinRAMPercentage=75.0 -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75.0 -XshowSettings:vm
   VM settings:
       Max. Heap Size (Estimated): 742.44M
       Using VM: Java HotSpot(TM) 64-Bit Server VM
   ```

5. Stop the container once ready.

   ```shell
   docker stop 'adjusted-heap'
   ```

6. Review the (default options) container file
   (`./containers/Dockerfile-Default-Options`)

   ```dockerfile
   FROM container-registry.oracle.com/java/jdk:25.0.4.1
   WORKDIR /opt/app

   ARG JAR_FILE=./target/java-command-line-options-spring-boot-1.0.0.jar

   COPY ${JAR_FILE} app.jar

   ENV JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS="-XshowSettings:vm"

   ENTRYPOINT ["java", "-jar", "app.jar"]
   ```

7. Build the (default options) container image

   ```shell
   docker build \
     --file './containers/Dockerfile-Default-Options' \
     --tag 'demo:default-options' \
     --load \
     .
   ```

8. Run the container image

   ```shell
   docker run \
     --rm \
     --detach \
     --memory=1G \
     --name 'default-options' \
     --publish 8080:8080 \
     'demo:default-options'
   ```

   Verify the amount of heap memory available to the application.

   ```shell
   docker logs 'default-options' | head
   ```

   This application is using 25% of memory available to the container.

   ```
   NOTE: Picked up JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS: -XshowSettings:vm
   VM settings:
       Max. Heap Size (Estimated): 247.50M
       Using VM: Java HotSpot(TM) 64-Bit Server VM
   ```

   This application is using 25% of memory available to the container.

9. Stop the container once ready.

   ```shell
   docker stop 'default-options'
   ```
